executiveSummary: GM0678 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but is not a calibrated Kapelle first-72-hour forecast. Kapelle lies between the Westerschelde and Oosterschelde, includes low polder land and the villages Kapelle/Biezelinge, Wemeldinge and Schore, and is crossed by the Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland, A58/Vlaketunnel, rail and provincial-road dependencies. The canonical coastal preset applies a broad 1.453748 legacy flood value and 5,818 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without selecting a Westerschelde or Oosterschelde boundary, defence section, breach/overtopping state or connected footprint. The major-river preset separately applies a persistent 0.671138 value through T+72 although no Rhine, Meuse or IJssel reach is named. Historic Hansweert breach analysis identifies a Schore/A58/Kapelle pathway, but the relevant 5.15-kilometre strengthening was completed and opened in May 2026, so the old study is mechanism evidence rather than a current footprint or warning. Eight unrelated presets reuse the same top-five neighbourhood order. Public sources identify 31 water-control assets, one sampled Stedin planning area, 18 antenna sites, 13 education records, a station and 24 transit stop areas, but provide no live hydraulic, utility, crossing, care or restoration state. Unsupported local precision must be suppressed or replaced by a named versioned scenario; empty or missing Waterinfo, NDW, weather, telecom-provider and acute-care records remain NoData or Unknown, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0678 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; BAG/PDOK and BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM0678 as Kapelle and report 13,012 residents, density 350 per square kilometre, 23.2% aged 65 or older and 1,649 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable fields retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [3.9627695185754144, 51.4822096028376] lies inside the 2025 generalized multipolygon. Six neighbourhoods occur in three districts. The loaded BAG intersection includes Kapelle, Kloetinge, Schore and Wemeldinge; BRT labels eight settlements under its own classification.

Neighbourhood populations sum to 13,015, three above the municipal total (+0.023%); generated allocation reconciles exactly to 13,012. Registers omit event-time tourists, canal/road/rail users, fruit-growing workers, commuters, care dependency and household emergency stocks.

evidenceSources.title: NWB, Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland, rail and scheduled public-transport context for Kapelle
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; current RWS waterway page
supports: Rijkswaterstaat describes the 11-kilometre Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland as a main waterway between the Westerschelde at Hansweert and Oosterschelde at Wemeldinge. The A58 passes beneath it through the Vlaketunnel near Kapelle; bridge and shipping operation are separate dependencies.

Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates seven logical links: A58 to Reimerswaal and Goes, N289 to Reimerswaal and Goes, N670 to Reimerswaal and Goes, and N666 to Borsele. Paired A58/N289/N670 edges share one physical corridor and their generalized 260/150 scenario capacities are not measured or additive emergency throughput.

One ProRail station, Kapelle-Biezelinge, and 24 GTFS stop areas are inside the deployment. Geometry and schedules do not establish event-time rail, bus, tunnel, bridge or canal operation, evacuation throughput, staffing, fuel or restoration.

No NDW situation is assigned within GM0678 in the deployment's bounded snapshot. That timestamp/coverage result does not establish that A58, Vlaketunnel, provincial roads, rail crossings or village approaches are open.

evidenceSources.title: Extended regional risk profile, current crisis plan and first-72-hour preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Crisisplan Zeeland 2026–2029; regional risk profile extended for 2023–2026; public guidance inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The crisis plan distinguishes the regional risk profile's question of what can threaten Zeeland from policy capacity and the crisis plan's organization of multidisciplinary response. These are governance and planning records, not a GM0678 warning, footprint, resource inventory, completed action or recovery commitment.

Zeeland Veilig includes flooding, extreme weather, utility failure, road/water/rail incidents and cyber disruption in its public hazard context. The extended profile covers 43 regional scenarios; inclusion does not validate the simulator's exact local magnitude, neighbourhood order or service curve.

The NCTV information booklet hosted by Zeeland Veilig advises preparation for 72 hours, including three litres of drinking water per person per day. It does not measure Kapelle household stocks or promise that authorities, hospitals, roads or utilities recover by T+72.
A 12 December 2024 Kapelle electrical-cabinet fire and associated partial outage is a dated incident observation, not evidence of a current outage or a calibration for every cyber or storm run.

evidenceSources.title: Sewerage, water-nuisance and public-space planning records
supports: The municipality's programme budget records village sewer basis plans from 2015–2017 and a 2019 Masterplan Wateroverlast that mapped known and project-level nuisance bottlenecks and solutions. In 2023 a successor municipal sewer plan for 2024–2028 was still being prepared.

The records describe periodic free-flow sewer inspection/cleaning, failure-driven pressure-main work, limited drain maintenance and monitored pumps maintained twice annually. Maintenance policy does not establish event-time capacity, obstruction, backup power, soil saturation or discharge acceptance.

The 2025 management report names current or planned water-nuisance and pump/pressure-main projects around Schelpenweg, Jagtlust/Van der Biltlaan, De Warretjes/Oude Bosstraat, Pronkenburg/Parklaan, Sterappelstraat and Opalstraat. Project status is static planning context, not a rain forecast or a completed protective effect unless explicitly verified.
No blanket machine-reuse licence was identified on these municipal documents.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Scheldestromen / Provincie Zeeland / Rijkswaterstaat-WMCN / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: Hansweert defence pathway, Zeeland flood/rain typology and public water-data routes
evidenceSources.edition: Hansweert project completed/opened 8 May 2026; Zeeland water programme published 2024; HWH/Waterinfo snapshots 2–3 September 2026; LIWO 2025.1.6
supports: Scheldestromen states that 5.15 kilometres of dike between Hansweert and Langeweg in Kapelle required height and inner-slope stability work, and that the completed strengthening was officially opened on 8 May 2026. The authority also cautions that prior noncompliance did not mean an acute unsafe situation. Completion is not a live defence observation or an all-flood all-clear.

The project's historic failure analysis describes water filling the polder to the A58, delayed passage beyond the motorway, later reach toward Kapelle and Wemeldinge, and high rise/depth risk in Hansweert and Schore. Because it concerns the pre-strengthening configuration, it is official scenario/mechanism evidence, not a current footprint, forecast or probability.

Provincial policy distinguishes primary-system flooding along the coast, Westerschelde and Oosterschelde; regional-defence flooding; unprotected regional water; groundwater; and intense-rain flooding anywhere. The Zeeland climate map separately offers return-period rain surfaces and an official 200-millimetre stress-test scenario. Scenario surfaces are not timestamped observations or forecasts.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 31 GM0678 points: three sewer pumps, two surface-water pumps, one wastewater treatment plant and 25 weirs. Twenty-six capacities are null; remaining values lack safe common unit/topology/state semantics. Twenty-seven objects name Scheldestromen, one uses generic 'Waterschap' and three have null manager.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned within GM0678 in the bounded snapshots. Empty point coverage is NoData, not zero water or an all-clear. LIWO 2025.1.6 is an irregular expert scenario library: a run must retain selected source water, level/hydrograph/datum, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Public provider territories, grid planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Provider/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1
supports: The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS identifies Stedin electricity and gas and Evides drinking water at the municipal reference point; provider dates range from December 2025 to May 2026, while drainage and telecom return empty. A point territory lookup is not municipality-wide completeness, physical topology, outage, quality, capacity or restoration.

The single sampled Stedin area TT228_10, Goes Evertsenstraat, has null existing and required capacity fields, 1.5 MW and 16 queued withdrawal requests, zero queued injection and twelve projects with earliest stated year 2026. NBNL planning is at least quarterly and queues monthly; its exact dataset licence was not found. It is not current load, reserve, customer availability or T+72 state.

RDI WFS returns 18 antenna sites, including eleven mobile and five fixed-link sites; no fixed refresh or blanket reuse licence was stated. Daily DUO RIO under CC BY (version unspecified) returns 13 education records. These do not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupancy, staff, supplies or live status.

RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026 under CC0, assigns no acute-care point to GM0678. Empty local count is not no acute-care need and does not establish which cross-boundary facility accepts a patient during an event.

evidenceSources.title: Cross-boundary acute care and drought/fresh-water context
evidenceSources.edition: Current Adrz and Scheldestromen pages; RIVM questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Adrz states that 24-hour acute and emergency care is provided at Goes. Its Goes page describes the region's only level-2 intensive care; RIVM records a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, 18 reported treatment rooms and 28,921 visits in 2025.

This establishes a plausible cross-boundary care dependency through the Goes road network, not incident-time acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup power, water, oxygen, medicines, ambulance availability or route passability.

Scheldestromen explains that Zeeland has few natural fresh-water sources, more short intense rainfall and extreme drought, and that fresh water is not always available. It is water-policy context, not a current drought observation, fruit-crop loss forecast or municipal drinking-water outage.

A historic Schore process-water reuse pilot served agricultural users during drought, but a dated pilot is not a current or guaranteed emergency supply. No blanket reuse licence was identified on the hospital and policy pages.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM0678 is uniquely Kapelle in Zeeland and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland.
Boundary/statistics editions are 2025; May 2026 dike completion, current registers, dated incidents and the synthetic model clock remain separate.
The reference point is contained and no headline mismatch was found.

geography.summary: Generalized municipal geometry is coherent, but estuary, canal, defence, polder and A58 pathways require full-resolution source geometry.
notes: Official evidence distinguishes Westerschelde/Oosterschelde primary-defence, regional-water and intense-rain pathways.
A municipal centroid or coast/river-distance scalar cannot replace selected defence sections, hydraulic connectivity, AHN terrain, A58/Vlaketunnel crossings, pumps and recession.
Every LIWO, climate-map, HWH and planning layer needs its own edition, valid time, scenario, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData mask.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and the small neighbourhood rounding difference is explicitly reconciled.
notes: Population 13,012, density 350, age65Pct 23.2 and one-person households 1,649 agree.
Neighbourhood population sums to 13,015 (+3); generated allocation reconciles to 13,012. Published neighbourhood households total 5,515 and age65+ rows total 3,005.
Older-resident and dispersed-village context does not measure who needs evacuation, cooling, transport, medicines or care.

regionalDetail.summary: All six neighbourhoods load, but several statistics and operational water/utility states are incomplete.
notes: District heat and public charging are missing for 6/6 neighbourhoods; home/housing/tenure fields for one and cars per household for two. Null is not zero.
HWH supplies 31 water points, but 26 capacities are null and non-null values cannot be summed without units, topology and current state.
Provider, planning, antenna, education and acute-care records do not establish event-time availability.

settlements.summary: Settlement context is useful, but BAG polygon intersection and BRT classification are not municipal population membership.
notes: The deployment lists four intersecting BAG woonplaatsen and eight BRT labels: Abbekinderen, Biezelinge, Dijkwel, Eversdijk, Kapelle, Maalstede, Schore and Wemeldinge.

Kloetinge is included by the BAG geometry intersection used for GM0678 while BRT assigns Kloetinge to neighbouring Goes; this must remain source-specific overlap semantics rather than duplicate residence or administrative membership.
Settlement labels must not duplicate CBS neighbourhood allocation or infer transient occupants.

transport.summary: Boundary road/rail inputs are reproducible, but canal, tunnel, bridge, station and external-care dependencies are absent from the causal network.
notes: Seven boundary edges represent four physical A/N corridors; paired A58, N289 and N670 edges are non-additive.
The Vlaketunnel, Vlakebrug/Postbrug, local canal approaches and rail crossings need event-valid state; an empty NDW subset is not open.
Kapelle-Biezelinge station and GTFS schedules do not guarantee emergency service, and Adrz Goes access/acceptance remains Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities, hazard types and dependencies are identifiable, but no auditable action/resource state exists for the first 72 hours.
notes: The model lacks selected source water/defence, rainfall, pump/weir, canal/tunnel/bridge/rail, warning trigger, authority, resource and completion state.
Adrz is a plausible regional dependency, not guaranteed capacity; access, acceptance, backup, oxygen, medicines and staffing remain Unknown.

Required actions include warning, defence/pump decisions, evacuation/reception, tunnel/bridge/road/rail control, care continuity, temporary water/sanitation, fruit-growing and livestock needs, utility repair, fuel/food/medicine distribution and mutual aid.
National 72-hour advice is not measured local preparedness or a recovery deadline.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: Mandatory and focused gates covered ten presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Outputs are synthetic exercise indices; affected people-equivalent is not observed people/casualties and person-hours is cumulative weighted local pre-network service shortfall versus a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0678 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across the complete matrix.
Intensity-zero event effects are zero, repeat runs and UI/core presets agree, and local allocation reconciles exactly.
Service-layer selection preserves physical hazard, route ceilings hold and event-attributable person-hours is monotonic.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Unselected coastal/river forcing and a repeated neighbourhood order contradict distinct estuary, polder, rain, heat and fire pathways.
notes: Coastal T+24 applies legacy floodDepthM diagnostic 1.453748 and 5,818 affected people-equivalent without source water, level/datum, primary defence, breach, footprint, arrival or recession.

River T+24 and T+72 retain floodDepthM diagnostic 0.671138 and severity 0.208667 without a named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach; Westerschelde/Oosterschelde, canal, regional water and pluvial mechanisms are separately typed and unresolved.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share Wemeldinge, Verspreide huizen Kapelle, Schore, Verspreide huizen Schore and Verspreide huizen Wemeldinge as the T+24 top five. The common order is not official exposure evidence.

The pre-strengthening Hansweert analysis identifies Schore as a high-risk pathway, while the generic rank puts Wemeldinge first; the historical study must not become a current footprint after the May 2026 strengthening.

Canonical wildfire has zero direct fire, 0.170829 smoke and 0.616423 drought without ignition, fuel, plume or time-valid fire-risk input; fruit-growing drought sensitivity is an indirect context, not simulated crop loss.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are inspectable but not calibrated to Scheldestromen assets, Stedin/Evides systems, crossings, rail or Adrz.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 0.496615, water 0.429142, drainage 0.271495, gas 0.697133, telecom 0.398233, mobility 0.812097, facilities 0.414598 and supply 0.842837; no authority/operator validates these exact values.
Stedin/Evides territory, one NBNL sample, HWH assets, RDI sites and normal schedules remain non-causal context.
NWB does not provide physical utility topology and omits internal canal/tunnel/bridge dependencies; Adrz registration does not establish incident access, acceptance or backup.
Sensitive or unavailable topology must use an explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, never invented public precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes exist, but unresolved water, defence, crossing, target and operational dimensions are not adequately declared.
notes: Coastal and river fields cannot be interpreted as measured metres without a selected hydraulic event, while compound reports a synthetic mix without selected defence, footprint, pump, crossing or recession state.

Cyber lacks a named target; wildfire lacks ignition/fuel/plume. Static context, a 2024 incident, annual registers, a completed 2026 project, current observations and synthetic T+72 values cannot be fused.
The 200-millimetre Zeeland stress-test is an official scenario, not an observation or forecast; the old Hansweert breach run is an official historic scenario, not the current defence configuration.
Empty Waterinfo, NDW, weather, drainage-provider, telecom-provider and local acute-care output must become explicit NoData/Unknown, not normal, open, safe or available.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and residual impacts lack hydraulic, operator, crossing, hospital or action evidence.
notes: Coastal direct severity and flood forcing return to zero by T+72, yet pressure remains 0.154009, affected people-equivalent 257 and person-hours 378,965.02; drainage availability is 0.706459 and facilities 0.857099 without recession, dewatering or restoration evidence.

River T+24 and T+72 retain severity 0.208667, flood diagnostic 0.671138, pressure 0.273685, 2,451 affected people-equivalent and identical service availability, while person-hours grow to 206,633.82; no selected event supports the plateau.
Compound pressure 0.548195, 7,483 affected people-equivalent and all eight service values remain exactly unchanged between T+24 and T+72 while person-hours grow from 125,536.74 to 477,690.89.

No defence/pump decision, tunnel/bridge/rail reopening, utility crew, Adrz acceptance, household stock or confirmed intervention supports those curves; 72 hours is a preparedness horizon, not an all-recovered promise.

findings.summary: The coastal preset presents an unselected estuary/primary-defence event as precise local flooding.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports legacy floodDepthM diagnostic 1.453748 and 5,818 affected people-equivalent without choosing Westerschelde or Oosterschelde water, level/datum, defence section, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, arrival, recession or probability.
findings.action: Suppress precise direct coastal impact unless an expert selects a versioned LIWO/Scheldestromen event. Preserve source water, boundary hydrograph/level/datum, wind, defence section/state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData.

findings.summary: The major-river preset falsely maps Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing onto Kapelle's different water systems.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports persistent floodDepthM diagnostic 0.671138 without a named major-river reach. Official Zeeland evidence instead distinguishes Westerschelde/Oosterschelde primary systems, regional/polder water, groundwater and intense rainfall.
findings.action: Suppress GM0678 direct impact in the generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset. Keep canal, estuary backwater, regional-water and indirect network pathways separately Unknown until a named connected event is selected; zero direct named-major-river forcing is not an all-flood all-clear.

findings.summary: One shared neighbourhood ranking substitutes for hazard-specific geometry.
findings.evidence: Eight unrelated presets reuse Wemeldinge, Verspreide huizen Kapelle, Schore, Verspreide huizen Schore and Verspreide huizen Wemeldinge in that order. Official historic Hansweert analysis instead identifies Schore-specific rise/depth and A58-delayed pathways, while rain, heat, cyber and fire require different evidence.
findings.action: Mark all nine local hazard distributions unsupported until source-specific layers replace the shared seed. Test coastal/regional flood, pluvial, wind, heat/drought and fire ranks independently; never reuse the historic pre-strengthening Hansweert footprint as current.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth and impact precision ignores available local stress-test and drainage evidence.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports legacy floodDepthM 0.203499 and 1,107 affected people-equivalent. Official sources identify village bottlenecks, pump/pressure-main projects, 31 partial water assets and provincial rain scenarios, but no hyetograph, AHN terrain, groundwater/saturation, sewer topology, pump state or footprint drives the result.
findings.action: Integrate a versioned municipal/Zeeland DPRA or 3Di surface with rainfall hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, groundwater/saturation, catchment/pump state, resolution, edition/licence, coverage and NoData; otherwise label local depth/rank/affected precision unsupported.

findings.summary: Exact utility and recovery percentages have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Coastal and compound return eight exact availability curves. Stedin/Evides territory, one grid-planning sample, HWH points and RDI registrations provide no live outage, connected topology, drinking-water quality, pump/control state, backup, switching, crew or repair evidence; drainage and telecom territory lookups are empty.
findings.action: Keep public context layers affectsSimulation=false and label operational values aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Ingest only authorized time-scoped operator aggregates and preserve manual incident-override provenance; empty and null values never mean zero, safe or available.

findings.summary: Thirty-one water assets are useful context but not an operational drainage model.
findings.evidence: HWH supplies three sewer pumps, two surface-water pumps, one wastewater plant and 25 weirs; 26 capacities are null and remaining values lack safe comparable units, connected catchments and current state.
findings.action: Retain every point, manager, null, collection, retrieval, licence and partial-coverage warning. Seek Scheldestromen-authorized catchment/control aggregates; never sum registered values or infer operating, backup or spare capacity.

findings.summary: Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland, Vlaketunnel, bridge, rail and village-access dependencies are missing.
findings.evidence: Kapelle's network crosses or follows a main waterway, A58 tunnel, movable bridges, rail and provincial roads, yet only seven generalized municipal boundary edges drive mobility. The local NDW snapshot is empty and schedules/geometry do not establish operation.
findings.action: Add critical crossing/approach identifiers with authority, event-valid open/restricted/closed/Unknown state, vehicle/rail/vessel class, restriction, capacity and alternate route. Keep paired road edges physically non-additive and propagate only confirmed crossing state to mobility and road logistics/supply.

findings.summary: Cross-boundary Adrz Goes acute-care access and acceptance are absent.
findings.evidence: No acute-care point lies in GM0678. RIVM and Adrz establish a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics and level-2 care in Goes, but not incident-time acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup, oxygen, medicines, ambulances or route availability.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate facility role, current acceptance/diversion, access, backup/fuel, critical supply and transfer state with valid time. Empty local count remains a cross-boundary dependency, not no demand; absent operational fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger connects authorities to recovery.
findings.evidence: Public sources identify responsible authorities, flood/rain mechanisms, water assets, crossings, an external SEH and household guidance, but the simulator ingests no warning trigger, assignment, resources, state or completion.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for warning, defence/pump decisions, evacuation/reception, tunnel/bridge/road/rail control, hospital continuity/transfer, temporary water/sanitation, food/fuel/medicine, fruit-growing/livestock needs, utility repair and mutual aid. Actions affect recovery only after confirmed status and provenance.

findings.summary: Non-flood hazard inclusion is bounded but not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: Wildfire reports zero direct fire but synthetic smoke/drought; earthquake has zero direct ground motion but nonzero burden; storm, heat, winter and cyber use synthetic forcing and the common neighbourhood order. Regional sources support scenario inclusion, not these exact values or local patterns.
findings.action: Retain presets only as clearly synthetic exercises with named forecast/observation valid time, target or ignition where relevant. Do not present zero direct earthquake/fire as an all-clear or infer observed smoke, heat, drought, ice, wind or cyber impact.

corrections.summary: Suppress unsupported GM0678 named-major-river inundation while preserving other water pathways as Unknown.
corrections.validation: The generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset produces zero GM0678 direct flood and direct affected population with an explicit unsupported-pathway note; Westerschelde/Oosterschelde, canal, regional-water, pluvial and indirect risks remain Unknown rather than safe.

corrections.summary: Gate coastal impact on a selected Westerschelde or Oosterschelde defence event and current defence configuration.
corrections.validation: No precise coastal result appears without a named versioned event; supported fixtures retain source water, boundary level/hydrograph/datum, wind, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, licence, coverage and NoData, and do not reuse the pre-May-2026 Hansweert configuration as current.

corrections.summary: Replace the common neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific flood, pluvial, weather, heat and fire geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated presets no longer share one top-five order; hydraulic fixtures follow selected connected scenarios, pluvial fixtures retain drainage/groundwater semantics and unresolved local distributions render Unknown rather than invented gradients.

corrections.summary: Keep water/provider/grid/antenna/education/acute-care records context-only with strict Unknown/NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: Cards and exports expose publisher, version, retrieval/valid time, licence, coverage, evidence class and affectsSimulation=false; null capacities and empty Waterinfo, NDW, weather, drainage-provider, telecom-provider and local acute-care outputs never render as zero, normal, safe, open or available.

corrections.summary: Represent canal/tunnel/bridge/rail, Adrz and role-aware first-72-hour actions in an Unknown-first ledger.
corrections.validation: At every checkpoint defences/pumps, warning/evacuation, crossing/road/rail access, hospital acceptance/transfer, reception/resupply and utility repair show authority, trigger, assignment, resource, state, source and valid time; only confirmed actions influence recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish Stedin/Evides/gas/telecom/drainage topology, current control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Flood consequences depend on selected Westerschelde or Oosterschelde level, defence section/configuration, breach/overtopping, polder/canal connectivity, pumps, terrain and recession; an historic breach study and a completed strengthening are not current event truth.
HWH asset coverage and capacity semantics vary; point geometry and registered values do not establish connected topology, comparable throughput, operating state or spare capacity.
RWS/ProRail/NWB/GTFS geometry and schedules do not establish event-time Vlaketunnel, bridge, canal, rail, bus or local-road operation, restriction or emergency throughput.

CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM records omit visitors, agricultural/seasonal workers, commuters, home-care needs, live hospital load, shelters and household stocks; BAG intersection is not necessarily administrative settlement membership.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, road, warning and facility states can change after audit completion; stale or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Separate Westerschelde/Oosterschelde primary-defence, Rhine/Meuse/IJssel major-river, regional-water/canal and intense-rain scenarios across Zeeland; never infer them from one centroid-distance field.

Reconcile Kapelle, Reimerswaal, Goes and Borsele flood and mobility pathways with one versioned LIWO/Scheldestromen/RWS contract, current defence configuration, A58/Vlaketunnel crossing semantics and explicit NoData.
Suppress GM0678's generic named-major-river false positive and gate broad coastal output on a selected estuary boundary and defence event.
Test the shared neighbourhood-ranking defect across estuary, polder, fruit-growing, heat, wind and rural-fire contexts with hazard-specific surfaces.
Audit A58/Vlaketunnel, N289/N670/N666, Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland bridges, rail and local approaches without double-counting paired NWB edges or converting schedules into guaranteed capacity.
Represent Adrz Goes and other regional care destinations through event-valid route access and acceptance, with Unknown-first water, evacuation, reception, resupply and repair actions.
